verdict.rationale: Helicone documents two event-triggered mechanisms. Webhooks fire when LLM requests complete, and you can filter them by property-match rules to automate downstream workflows. Alerts watch error rates and costs, using filters to notify through Slack or email. Both are narrow: the documented event is request completion or a metric threshold, and the actions are limited to an HTTP callback or a notification, not a general rule builder. Missing for 10: a general-purpose rule/condition engine across multiple event types, a choice of built-in actions beyond callbacks and notifications, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Webhooks provide instant notifications when LLM requests complete, allowing you to automate workflows, score responses, and integrate AI activity with external systems.
Only requests matching ALL specified properties will trigger webhooks.
Each alert can be configured with filters and automatically notify through channels like Slack or email.
Helicone Alerts let you monitor error rates and costs on LLM requests to catch issues before they impact users.
